transcript_tail.text: Let me check the bucketed scan now.

The fast scan deadlocked (classic pipe-buffer deadlock: I wrote all stdin before reading stdout). I don't need it — I have BEFORE (1189/107/8) and AFTER-13path (25/93), and the file lists already tell the story. Let me kill it and run one targeted check: confirm the real (non-vendor) emails baked into stays-on-HEAD source/test/docs are essentially just the owner's, which sets the `--replace-text` scope.

Decisive: in the **stays-on-HEAD source/test/doc files**, the only emails in history are **the owner's own** (`jdtogni@gmail.com`, 2 variants, ~138 occurrences) — the #81 residual. So:
- **Real family-member PII** (the ~15 family emails + their hashes) lives *only* in the purgeable data files (dumps, datadir, users CSV) → removed by path-purge.
- **Stays-on-HEAD files** need only `--replace-text` of the owner email.
- The other ~90 history emails are **open-source author emails** in legacy `php_app2/vendor/*` (public, not PII) → optional legacy-dir purge clears the noise + bloat.

That's a complete, clean characterization. Let me finalize the audit doc with the real numbers and the precise two-part recipe.
Now let me refine §4 (the recipe) and §5 (execution) to reflect the complete two-part recipe + the dry-run numbers I proved.

Let me sanitize one example in the audit doc — I shouldn't write a literal `DB_PASSWORD=<value>` assignment into a *new* tracked file (that's exactly the hygiene we're enforcing, and could trip the gitleaks pre-commit hook).

The audit is complete and documented. I've written three artifacts to the worktree (uncommitted):
- `docs/security/HISTORY-AUDIT-66.md` — full report
- `docs/security/history-purge-paths.txt` — validated 14-path purge spec
- `docs/security/SECURITY-EXPOSURE.md` — §5/§7 updated with results

Here's where #66 stands before I touch anything outward-facing.

## Audit result — history is NOT clean (publishing now would leak)

Scanned **all 1027 commits across every ref** (the published surface is wide: main + `claude/*`, `codex-*`, all `dependabot/*`, several `feature/*` and pushed `worktree-*`). The project `.gitleaks.toml` *allowlists* the leaked dev creds (right for the working-tree CI scan, wrong for a history audit), so I scanned with a strict config + a full-blob PII sweep.

**Whole-history exposure: ~1189 bcrypt hashes, ~107 emails, 8 leaked APP_KEYs across 207 files**, which split cleanly:

| Where it lives | Content | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `app1/datadir_acl/` (**253 objects** — raw InnoDB `.ibd`/`.frm` tables, `ibdata1`) | real rows: hashes + emails | **path-purge** |
| SQL dumps (`familyfund_dump.sql`, `*_data.sql`, `test-baseline.sql.gz`, …) | hashes + ~15 **family-member** emails | **path-purge** |
| leaked `.env.dev`/`.env.local`/`.env.test0` | leaked APP_KEY + DB pw (**already rotated → dead**) | **path-purge** |
| `database/csv/familyfund_users.csv` (7-user export) | emails + hashes — *I'd missed this; now added* | **path-purge** |
| source/tests/docs on HEAD | only the **owner's own email** (`jdtogni@gmail.com`; HEAD already parameterized by #81, history isn't) | **`--replace-text`** |
| dead `php_app2/vendor/**` etc. | ~90 open-source **author** emails (public, not PII) + bloat | optional legacy-dir purge |

**Working tree (HEAD) is effectively clean** — every dump/env/CSV is already removed; the two kept scripts (`prod_to_dev.sql`, `restore_dev_funds.sql`) carry only synthetic/functional residuals.

## Purge validated (non-destructive dry-run on a mirror clone)

Live repo & `origin` untouched. Path-purge on the clone: **`datadir_acl` 253→0, APP_KEYs 8→0**, 7 now-empty commits dropped, every path confirmed gone. Tool (`git-filter-repo`) is installed and works.

## The gated part

The actual purge = **history rewrite + force-push of all branches**. Blast radius: every clone, the ~50 local worktree branches, all pushed `origin` branches, and the pool/test envs diverge and must re-clone/hard-reset — and concurrent agent sessions use those. Since the dev creds are already rotated (dead), the residual risk being remediated is **PII + offline-crackable hashes**, and this is only required *before going public* (#68, currently blocked). So there's no urgency forcing it now.
